description: From-scratch LLM inference engine: C++20 core (no deps), Python bindings + benchmark harness. Model: Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct (Apache-2.0, ungated). Features are sequenced; dependencies flow forward.

features.description: Project builds clean with warnings-as-errors on Apple clang (C++20, -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror) and ctest runs
steps: Run `cmake -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release`
Run `cmake --build build -j` and verify zero warnings/errors
Run `ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure` and verify it executes

features.description: init.sh verifies toolchain, builds, and runs ctest green end-to-end
steps: Run `bash init.sh` from the repo root
Verify it checks cmake + compiler versions
Verify it configures, builds, and runs ctest
Verify it reports model presence/absence and exits 0 on a healthy tree

features.description: Model download script fetches Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct (ungated, Apache-2.0) into git-ignored models/
steps: Run `scripts/download_model.sh` on a clean tree
Verify config.json, tokenizer files, and model.safetensors (~1GB) land in models/qwen2.5-0.5b-instruct/
Verify re-running skips already-downloaded files
Verify `git status` shows nothing from models/

features.description: GitHub Actions CI (ubuntu + macos) builds and runs ctest; model-dependent tests skip cleanly without weights
steps: Push repo to GitHub (user action) with .github/workflows/ci.yml present
Verify both ubuntu-latest and macos-latest jobs go green
Verify model-dependent tests report SKIPPED, not FAILED, in CI logs

features.description: Minimal JSON parser (no deps) handles safetensors headers, config.json, and vocab.json including \uXXXX escapes
steps: Run test_json via ctest
Verify parsing of objects, arrays, strings, ints, floats, bools, null
Verify unicode escape decoding (incl. surrogate pairs) to UTF-8
Verify malformed input is rejected with a clear error, not a crash

features.description: safetensors loader: mmap the file, parse header, expose tensors by name with dtype/shape, validate all offsets in bounds
steps: Run test_safetensors via ctest with real downloaded weights
Verify tensor count and total parameter count match Qwen2.5-0.5B (~494M params)
Verify model.embed_tokens.weight has shape [151936, 896] and dtype BF16
Verify a corrupted/truncated header is rejected with a clear error

features.description: bf16 -> fp32 conversion is bit-exact vs a numpy golden vector from the real weights
steps: Regenerate tests/data/embed_golden.json with scripts/gen_golden.py
Run test_safetensors via ctest
Verify the first N converted values of model.embed_tokens.weight match the golden values exactly

features.description: config.json parses into a typed ModelConfig (hidden size, layers, heads, kv heads, rope theta, norm eps, vocab size)
steps: Run test_config via ctest with the real config.json
Verify hidden_size=896, layers=24, heads=14, kv_heads=2, vocab=151936 for Qwen2.5-0.5B
Verify missing required fields produce a clear error

features.description: CLI `nanoserve inspect <file.safetensors>` prints a tensor table (name, dtype, shape) plus parameter/byte totals
steps: Run `./build/nanoserve inspect models/qwen2.5-0.5b-instruct/model.safetensors`
Verify a readable table is printed with all tensors
Verify totals line reports parameter count and file size
Verify a helpful error (not a crash) on a nonexistent or invalid file

features.description: Byte-level BPE tokenizer loads vocab.json + merges.txt (GPT-2 style byte-to-unicode mapping, ranked merges)
steps: Run test_tokenizer via ctest with real tokenizer files
Verify vocab size is 151643 base entries (Qwen2.5) and merges load without error

features.description: encode() matches HF tokenizers exactly on an English/ASCII golden corpus (20+ prompts incl. punctuation, numbers, whitespace, newlines)
steps: Regenerate tests/data/tokenizer_golden.json with scripts/gen_golden.py (uses the real tokenizer.json via the tokenizers library)
Run test_tokenizer via ctest
Verify every prompt's token ids match the golden ids exactly

features.description: decode() inverts encode(): roundtrip is byte-identical for the whole golden corpus
steps: Run test_tokenizer via ctest
Verify decode(encode(s)) == s for every corpus prompt
Verify decoding golden ids reproduces the original prompt text

features.description: Special tokens (<|im_start|>, <|im_end|>, <|endoftext|>) are recognized atomically and a Qwen chat-template helper builds correct prompt ids
steps: Add chat-template cases to gen_golden.py (apply_chat_template reference ids)
Run test_tokenizer via ctest
Verify special tokens encode to their single reserved ids, never split into bytes
Verify the chat-template helper's ids match the HF reference ids

features.description: Full Unicode pretokenizer parity: encode matches HF on CJK, accented text, and emoji corpus
steps: Extend the golden corpus with non-ASCII prompts (CJK, Cyrillic, emoji, mixed)
Run test_tokenizer via ctest
Verify exact id match on every non-ASCII prompt

features.description: Core fp32 ops with unit tests vs numpy goldens: matmul (row-major GEMV/GEMM), rmsnorm, softmax, silu, elementwise add/mul
steps: Add op golden cases to scripts/gen_golden.py
Run test_ops via ctest
Verify each op matches numpy within 1e-5 relative tolerance on random inputs of representative shapes

features.description: RoPE (rotary position embeddings, Qwen2 half-rotation layout, theta=1e6) matches a HF reference implementation
steps: Generate RoPE golden vectors from the HF Qwen2 implementation
Run test_ops via ctest
Verify rotated q/k match within 1e-5 for several positions and head dims

features.description: Single transformer layer forward (attention with GQA + MLP) matches HF layer output for a real input
steps: Generate a golden: hidden states in/out of layer 0 from HF transformers for a fixed prompt
Run test_forward via ctest
Verify layer output matches within 1e-4 relative tolerance

features.description: Full fp32 forward pass: prompt -> logits matches HF within tolerance; argmax token identical
steps: Generate golden logits (final position) from HF transformers for 3 fixed prompts
Run test_forward via ctest
Verify top-1 token id matches exactly and logits match within 1e-3 relative tolerance

features.description: Greedy decoding end-to-end: `nanoserve generate` produces the same continuation as HF greedy for fixed prompts (32+ tokens)
steps: Generate HF greedy continuations for 3 chat prompts via gen_golden.py
Run `./build/nanoserve generate models/qwen2.5-0.5b-instruct -p <prompt> -n 32 --greedy`
Verify the generated token ids match the HF reference exactly
Run test_generate via ctest covering the same check

features.description: KV cache: incremental decode produces identical logits to full-recompute decode, and is measurably faster per token
steps: Run test_kvcache via ctest
Verify per-step logits with cache == logits recomputing the full sequence (exact match)
Verify per-token wall time with cache is lower than without for a 128-token generation (assert, and print both numbers)

features.description: Prefill/decode split with timing hooks: engine reports time-to-first-token and per-token decode latency
steps: Run `nanoserve generate ... --stats`
Verify TTFT (prefill) and mean/median decode ms/token are printed
Verify the numbers are plausible and stable across two runs (within 20%)

features.description: Sampling: temperature, top-k, top-p with a seeded RNG; deterministic given a seed
steps: Run test_sampling via ctest
Verify temperature=0 equals greedy
Verify top-k/top-p restrict the candidate set correctly on hand-built distributions
Verify two runs with the same seed produce identical outputs, different seeds differ

features.description: Streaming: tokens are emitted to a callback as generated; CLI prints them incrementally with correct UTF-8 handling at token boundaries
steps: Run `nanoserve generate ... ` and verify tokens appear incrementally, not all at once
Verify multi-byte UTF-8 characters split across tokens render correctly
Run test_streaming via ctest verifying callback ordering and byte-exact final text

features.description: No heap allocations in the decode hot loop (buffers preallocated from config); verified by an allocation counter in debug builds
steps: Run test_alloc via ctest
Verify allocation count during 16 decode steps is zero after warmup
Verify generation output is unchanged from before the refactor

features.description: Multithreaded matmul via a persistent thread pool; >=2.5x speedup over single-thread on 8+ perf cores with identical outputs
steps: Run test_ops via ctest (threaded matmul matches single-thread outputs exactly per reduction order or within 1e-5)
Run bench/ops microbenchmark: record single-thread vs threaded GEMV time for the lm_head shape
Verify >=2.5x speedup and record the measured number in the progress log
Verify end-to-end generate output is unchanged

features.description: SIMD kernels (NEON on arm64, with scalar fallback) for dot/matmul/rmsnorm; measured speedup with correctness tests
steps: Run test_ops via ctest: SIMD results match scalar within 1e-5
Run bench/ops microbenchmark: record scalar vs SIMD numbers
Verify speedup > 1.5x on the GEMV shapes and record measured numbers in the progress log
Verify the scalar fallback path still compiles and passes on x86 CI

features.description: int8 weight quantization (per-row scales, offline pass) with quantized matmul; quality checked, speed measured
steps: Run `nanoserve quantize` (or script) to produce an int8 weight file
Run test_quant via ctest: dequantized weights within expected error; forward top-1 unchanged on golden prompts
Measure tok/s fp32 vs int8 with the bench harness and record both numbers
Verify greedy continuations on the 3 golden prompts are unchanged (or document divergence honestly)

features.description: pybind11 bindings: `import nanoserve; nanoserve.Engine(model_dir).generate(prompt, max_tokens=...)` works from Python
steps: Run `pip install -e .` (scikit-build-core) in the venv
Run `python -c "import nanoserve; print(nanoserve.Engine('models/qwen2.5-0.5b-instruct').generate('Hello', max_tokens=8))"`
Verify output matches the CLI for the same settings
Run the Python-side pytest in tests/python/

features.description: Python streaming API: generate(..., stream=True) yields tokens as they are produced, with stats (ttft, tok/s) on the result object
steps: Run the streaming example in tests/python/
Verify tokens arrive incrementally (timestamps recorded per token)
Verify result.ttft_ms and result.tokens_per_second are populated and plausible

features.description: Python benchmark harness: measures prefill TTFT and decode tok/s over fixed prompt/generation lengths, N repeats with warmup, writes JSON + pretty table
steps: Run `python bench/run.py --engine nanoserve --repeats 5`
Verify JSON results land in bench/results/ with machine info (chip, core count, RAM)
Verify a readable table (mean +/- std) is printed
Verify repeat-to-repeat variance < 10% or flagged in output

features.description: llama.cpp comparison: same model, same machine, matched settings (threads, context, fp32/quant level), driven by the same harness
steps: Build llama.cpp at a pinned commit via bench/setup_llamacpp.sh; convert/download the matched GGUF
Run `python bench/run.py --engine llama.cpp --repeats 5` with matched settings
Verify the harness records llama.cpp version, build flags, and settings in the JSON
Verify a combined comparison table prints both engines side by side

features.description: README benchmark section auto-generated from bench results: reproducible command, hardware disclosure, honest gap statement vs llama.cpp
steps: Run `python bench/report.py` to regenerate the README table from bench/results/
Verify the README shows tok/s + TTFT for nanoserve and llama.cpp with the exact repro command and hardware/versions
Verify no number in the README was hand-typed (all injected from results JSON)

features.description: Metal backend for the matmul path (M-series GPU), parity-tested against CPU, benchmarked with the same harness
steps: Run test_metal via ctest on macOS (skips elsewhere): GPU matmul matches CPU within 1e-3
Run generate with --backend metal and verify identical greedy output on golden prompts
Benchmark CPU vs Metal with bench/run.py and record both

features.description: Paged KV cache: fixed-size blocks with a free-list allocator, enabling long generations without preallocating max context
steps: Run test_kvcache paged cases via ctest: outputs identical to the contiguous cache
Verify memory high-water mark for a short generation is much lower than the full-context preallocation (print both)
Verify a generation that exceeds one block boundary is still exact

features.description: HTTP serving endpoint: POST /v1/completions (subset of the OpenAI schema) with streaming (SSE), served from the C++ engine
steps: Run `nanoserve serve models/qwen2.5-0.5b-instruct --port 8080`
Run `curl localhost:8080/v1/completions -d '{...}'` and verify a well-formed completion response
Verify stream:true produces SSE chunks token by token
Run test_server via ctest (spawns server, requests, checks response)

features.description: Continuous batching in the server: two concurrent requests share decode steps; throughput improves vs serial
steps: Fire 4 concurrent requests at the server and verify all complete correctly
Verify combined throughput exceeds serial execution of the same 4 requests (print both)
Verify single-request latency does not regress beyond 20%
